variables.name: participant_id
variables.label: Study participant ID
variables.notes: A random study code assigned by the research team. Never use a student ID number, email, or name. Keep the linking key separately from the data, and replace these codes with new random codes before sharing.

variables.name: timepoint
variables.label: Data collection timepoint
variables.notes: For long-format data. In wide-format data, use the _pre / _post / _t1 ... suffixes on variable names instead.

variables.name: age_years
variables.label: Age in years
variables.question: What is your age in years?
variables.notes: Consider collecting or sharing age in ranges, and top-coding older ages, to reduce re-identification risk.

variables.name: race_eth
variables.label: Race and/or ethnicity (combined question)
variables.question: What is your race and/or ethnicity?
variables.source: OMB Statistical Policy Directive No. 15 (2024), minimum reporting categories
variables.notes: Each option is stored as its own 0/1 variable (race_eth_aian, race_eth_asian, ...). SPD 15 also calls for detailed categories and write-in fields under each minimum category; add those as study-specific variables when collected. 'Prefer not to answer' is a HuMeta addition, not an SPD 15 category. Small groups can identify individuals: check cell sizes before sharing.

variables.name: consent_share
variables.label: Consented to data sharing
variables.question: Do you agree that your de-identified responses may be shared with other researchers?
variables.notes: Only participants coded 1 may be included in any shared dataset. Wording must match the IRB-approved consent form.
